messages.subject: MSstats results
messages.body_plain:
Hi I have some question about MSstats results.

I am trying to draw the multi-biomarker ROC curves based on the abundance results from Skyline.
I used MSstats to gain differnetially expressed proteins and want to see the correlation between multi-marker ROC curves and MSstats results.

Therefore, is there any ways to get "normalized" abundance data (ratio between heavy and endogenous peptides)??
I think some data is marked on dataProcessedData excel file but, I am not sure which data I have to use.

Can I export normalized abundance data from MSstats results??

I appreciate for your help.

messages.subject: Re: MSstats results
messages.body_plain:
The normalized endogenous abundance data is available by command-line in R. (currently it is not one of the outputs from external tool in Skyline.

x <- dataProcess(something)

Then, x$RunlevelData includes Run-level summarized data (normalized endogenous abundance by reference). However, it is still not the ratio between heavy and endogenous peptides. MSstats does not report the ratio.

HTH

- Meena

messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi HFaz,

Current MSstatsTMT doesn't support gene names as protein names for the MaxQuant output. But we have put this suggestion in our future work calendar.

As a temporary solution, I have revised the MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat() function to support gene names and attached the function code. Now you can read in the "MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2.R" script, call function MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2() to do preprocessing, and then run MSstatsTMT to do the following analysis.

Here is an example:

library(MSstatsTMT)
source("MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2.R")

input.mq <http://input.mq> <- MaxQtoMSstatsTMTFormat2(evidence = evidence,
                                    proteinGroups = proteinGroups,
                                    annotation = annotation.mq <http://annotation.mq>,
                                    which.proteinid = 'Gene.names')
head(input.mq <http://input.mq>)

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MastatsTMT question with annotation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dezi,

The evidence file of MaxQuant is the table with identified peptide features. It should have the channel columns, such as

Reporter intensity corrected X, where X is the index of the “tag”, starting with 0
Reporter intensity X
Reporter intensity count X

If your evidence file doesn't have those channel columns, then there maybe something wrong when you output the results. See this introduction to MaxQuant: https://www.labkey.org/Documentation/wiki-page.view?name=maxQuant. It shows how to get and view the evidence file.

Best,

Ting

messages.subject: !! The May Institute - Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics at NEU in 2019
messages.subject_clean: !! The May Institute - Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics at NEU in 2019
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats Users,

I am pleased to announce that May institute - Computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics at NEU in 2019 has opened the application.

The May Institute on Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics, taking place on April 29 – May 10, 2019 on campus of Northeastern University in Boston MA, is now accepting applications. The application deadline is January 31, 2019. Participants can select a subset of the following programs:

- Targeted proteomics with Skyline

- Proteomics and metabolomics with OpenMS

- [NEW THIS YEAR!] Imaging mass spectrometry with Cardinal

- Beginner’s statistics in R

- Advanced R

- Statistics for quantitative mass spectrometry

- Visualization of biomolecular data

- [NEW THIS YEAR!] Scientific writing

- Capstone – case studies in data-independent acquisition (DIA)

Instructors are leading experts, who contributed numerous experimental and computational methods and software. The target audience are both beginners and experienced scientists, with both experimental and computational expertise.

Tuition fee wavers and travel fellowships will be available for students and postdocs affiliated with academic institutions in the US.

More information is at https://computationalproteomics.ccis.northeastern.edu/

It is great opportunity for MSstats users to discuss with MSstats teams. Also there are more interesting topics for bench scientist and bioinformaticians. We look forward to seeing you at this course.

- Meena
